title: Zoom! Swimmers Smash Records in Fastest 50-Meter Butterfly Race Ever
summary: Have you ever tried to swim across a pool as fast as you can? Now imagine doing it with just your arms and a dolphin kick, flying like a butterfly. That's the 50-meter butterfly, and at the European Championships, swimmers turned the pool into a rocket launchpad! In the semi-finals, the water practically boiled as racers shattered records left and right. The star was Egor Kornev from Russia, who zoomed to a time of 22.36 seconds. That's faster than you can say 'supercalifragilisticexpialidocious'! He broke the championship record and is now the third-fastest man in history. He's chasing the world record of 22.27 seconds, set by Andriy Govorov. But Kornev wasn't alone. Seven other swimmers set national records for their countries. Maxime Grousset of France and Noe Ponti of Switzerland came super close to their own records, missing by just a blink — 0.01 and 0.02 seconds! The competition was so fierce that a time of 22.75 seconds was needed just to make the final. That's faster than the time that won medals at past championships. In fact, 11 swimmers went faster than the old bronze-medal time. It was like a video game where everyone suddenly unlocked a speed boost. The final promises to be a showdown of the fastest butterflies on the planet. So grab your goggles and imagine the splash — these athletes are redefining what's possible in the water!
why_it_matters: Seeing athletes smash records shows that hard work and practice can lead to amazing results. If you stay dedicated to your sport or hobby, you might one day break your own personal records and inspire others.

background_read: The European Swimming Championships bring top athletes from across the continent together to compete. The 50-meter butterfly is one of the shortest and fastest pool races, and winning often comes down to a fraction of a second.

World and national records are broken when swimmers combine perfect technique, explosive power, and sometimes high-tech swimsuits. Egor Kornev (a Russian swimmer) is now chasing the world record set by Andriy Govorov (a Ukrainian swimmer) in 2018.
Article_Structure: WHO: Russian swimmer Egor Kornev, along with other top European swimmers.
WHAT: Kornev broke the championship record in the 50-meter butterfly semi-finals, and many national records fell as well.
WHERE: At the European Championships, a major swimming competition.
WHY: Because the level of competition was incredibly high—11 swimmers were faster than the old bronze-medal time, pushing everyone to swim at record-breaking speeds.

perspectives.description: Swimmers feel proud and excited to see their years of training pay off. Setting a national or championship record is a huge moment that shows they’re among the best in the world.
Coaches see these fast times as proof that training methods are working better than ever. It pushes them to find new ways to help swimmers go even faster in future races.
Watching a race where many records fall is thrilling. It makes young fans believe that records are meant to be broken and encourages them to take up swimming or any sport they love.
